background: Rentenbank is Germany's development bank for agriculture and rural areas, a federal institution carrying an explicit guarantee from the German state, which funds itself in the bond markets and lends through other banks to farms, food businesses and rural infrastructure.
synthesis: Ratings are AAA from Fitch and S&P and Aaa from Moody's, matching the German sovereign that guarantees it. Capital is mixed against EU and Nordic peers on the two measures held: CET1 of 28.4% is in the top quarter against the peer median, while leverage of 5.0% is below the peer median, a normal shape for a wholesale lender with very low risk weights. CET1 has risen 5.7 points since 30 Jun 2016 and leverage 1.0 points since 31 Dec 2016, but the figures run only to 30 Jun 2018, so they are very old. Nothing has been flagged in the last 90 days. The federal guarantee is what a depositor is relying on.
